children.text: Generally, when an argument reaches enough people in a public sphere, it gets so big that debaters lose sight of the main issue and start to go down rabbit holes of other important issues, other less important issues, or the good ol’ fashion fun of getting mad at other people online.
N.B.: Many time, derailment is obvious! Here, none of these issues are outlandishly off topic – instead, they lack specificity or perhaps shift the focus to other related, but less relevant issues.
Key Moment #1: First Amendment Free Speech vs. Free Speech in General
The biggest derailment of this debate is the ongoing misunderstanding of the first amendment.

Watch the video below that explains why it's not a matter of violating the first amendment but rather transparent and fair application of moderation policies by private entities -- not the government.
Key Moment #2: Cancel Culture vs. Moderation
With key figures getting banned from social media platforms, the question of whether platforms where engaging in “cancel culture” or simply moderating content according to their policies arose.
to read research from the Pew Research Center about how Americans view and define cancel culture.
Ongoing Moment: People Making Fun of Others on the Internet

And of course, people began making memes about Elon Musk, who bought Twitter in 2022. Some viewed the purchase as an effort to champion free speech and reduce censorship. Others, however, saw it as placing a major public forum under the control of a single wealthy billionaire – one they believed had an inconsistent and potentially dangerous understanding of free speech.
